summary: In this excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 2, part 167), the narrator and Rio discover that all electronics have failed, which Rio attributes to an EMP attack. Checker explains that a high-altitude nuclear detonation could cause such an effect, and the narrator worries about cars and cloud backups. A radio broadcast reports an unverified 'event' localized to Southern California, parts of Arizona, Nevada, and Mexico, with FEMA and the National Guard deployed. Rio and the narrator conclude the attack is a stalling tactic meant to let their pursuers hunt them down.
one_line: In a fiction novel, the characters learn that an EMP attack has knocked out electronics across Southern California and beyond, likely to stall their pursuit.
key_facts: Rio reinserted the battery into the burner cell, pressed the power button, and got no response.
Rio said, "Not a power outage," and attributed the failure to an EMP attack that Pithica launched to protect itself after alerts went out.
Checker said a high-altitude nuclear detonation is probably the easiest way to produce an EMP.
Checker said one high-altitude nuke could take out all the electronics in the United States.
Checker said no loss of human life would result directly, except for people depending on medical electronics.
The narrator asked, "What about cars?" and Checker replied that most cars are computerized these days.
Checker said that backups in the cloud should be fine through distributed computing, depending on how much had been taken out.
Rio found a working radio kept inside a Faraday cage in a metal box.
A radio broadcast said it was unverified whether the event was an attack or a natural phenomenon.
The President asked people to help each other out and avoid panic, and FEMA and the National Guard were being deployed to affected areas.
The event was at least localized to Southern California and parts of Arizona, Nevada, and Mexico.
Rio said, "This is not their endgame," and the narrator agreed it was a stalling tactic.
Rio said the enemy would have some plan of escalation and was very efficient when pooling resources.
The narrator suspected the attackers were provoked by what Steve's group did and tracked it back to them.
